body_markdown:
UK shoppers are being urged to check their cupboards after two popular Dubai-style chocolate products were recalled following the detection of Salmonella.


World of Sweets has recalled two chocolate products sold in the UK as a precautionary measure. Consumers who have purchased the affected chocolates have been advised not to eat them and to return them to the retailer for a refund.


The recall involves Dubai-style chocolate products containing pistachio and knafeh, a combination that has become increasingly popular with chocolate lovers.


## Which Chocolate Products Have Been Recalled?


The affected products are:


- Dubai Style Crunchy Knafeh and Pistachio Milk Chocolate, 100g
- Alyan Dubai Style Chocolate Truffles, 120g


According to the product recall information, Salmonella was detected in the affected chocolate.


World of Sweets has advised customers who purchased the products not to consume them. The company is also encouraging consumers to handle the affected packaging carefully and keep it away from other food products to reduce the possibility of cross-contamination.


Anyone who believes they have purchased one of the recalled products should check the packaging and any available recall information to confirm whether their chocolate is affected.


## What Should Shoppers Do With the Recalled Chocolate?


Consumers should not eat chocolate covered by the recall.


Instead, shoppers can return the affected product to the store where it was purchased. Customers are expected to be offered a full refund in accordance with the recall instructions.


People who purchased an affected product directly from World of Sweets can contact the company's customer support service for information about what to do next.


Consumers should also avoid allowing the recalled product or its packaging to come into unnecessary contact with other food.


Point-of-sale notices are expected to be displayed by retailers that stocked the affected chocolates. These notices provide customers with details about the recall and instructions on what they should do if they have purchased the product.


## Why Has the Chocolate Been Recalled?


The recall was issued after Salmonella was detected.


Salmonella is a type of bacteria that can cause food poisoning. Contaminated food does not necessarily look, smell or taste unusual, which is one reason official food recalls should be taken seriously.


Food businesses can recall products when a potential safety issue is identified. A recall allows products that have already reached consumers to be removed from circulation while customers are informed about the possible risk.


In this case, the advice is straightforward: consumers with an affected product should not eat it.


## What Are the Symptoms of Salmonella?


Salmonella infection can cause a number of gastrointestinal symptoms.


Common symptoms can include diarrhoea, fever, nausea, vomiting and abdominal cramps. The severity and duration of illness can vary from person to person.


Symptoms of food poisoning can sometimes be managed at home, particularly by resting and making sure enough fluids are consumed to reduce the risk of dehydration.


However, some people can become more seriously unwell. Anyone experiencing severe or concerning symptoms should seek appropriate medical advice.


People who suspect they have an infection should also take precautions to reduce the risk of spreading illness to other people, particularly through careful handwashing and good hygiene.


Official NHS guidance should be consulted for current advice on food poisoning symptoms, treatment and when to seek medical assistance.


## Why Product Recalls Matter


Food recalls are an important part of the UK's food safety system.


Manufacturers, suppliers and retailers can remove a product from sale when a safety problem is discovered. Depending on the circumstances, customers who have already purchased the product may then be advised to return or dispose of it.


Potential microbiological contamination is particularly important because harmful microorganisms may not produce obvious signs that food is unsafe.


This means consumers should not rely on appearance, smell or taste to decide whether a recalled product is safe.


If the batch or product in your home matches an official recall notice, following the recall instructions is the safest course of action.


## Dubai-Style Chocolate Has Become Hugely Popular


Dubai-style chocolate has attracted significant attention in recent years, particularly on social media.


The trend is commonly associated with chocolate bars featuring rich pistachio fillings and crispy knafeh or kataifi-style pastry. Videos showing the distinctive green pistachio filling have helped turn the confectionery style into a recognisable trend.


Numerous manufacturers and retailers have subsequently introduced their own versions of pistachio-filled and knafeh-inspired chocolate products.


The current recall relates to the specific products identified in the recall notice. It should not be interpreted as a warning against all Dubai-style chocolate or all pistachio chocolate products.


Consumers should therefore check product names, packaging and official recall details rather than assuming that similar products from other manufacturers are affected.


## How to Check Whether Food Has Been Recalled


Anyone concerned about a product in their kitchen should check official food safety alerts and the manufacturer's recall information.


Recall notices typically identify important details such as the product name, pack size, affected batch or date information where applicable, the reason for the recall and the action consumers should take.


Shoppers should compare these details carefully with the packaging they have at home.


It is also worth paying attention to notices displayed in supermarkets. Retailers frequently place recall information near entrances, customer service areas or locations where an affected product was previously sold.


Consumers should avoid eating a product while they are trying to establish whether it is included in a safety recall.


## What to Do If You Have Already Eaten the Chocolate


Eating a recalled product does not automatically mean that a person will become ill.


However, anyone who has consumed an affected product should be aware of possible symptoms associated with Salmonella infection.


If symptoms develop, follow current NHS guidance. People experiencing severe symptoms, signs of significant dehydration or other concerning health problems should seek medical advice.


Extra care may also be appropriate for people who could be more vulnerable to complications from foodborne illness.


The key message for anyone who still has one of the affected chocolate products is not to consume it and to follow the retailer or manufacturer's recall instructions.


## Shoppers Encouraged to Check Their Cupboards


The recall is another reminder of why consumers should pay attention to food safety alerts, even for packaged products such as confectionery.


Anyone who recently purchased Dubai-style pistachio or knafeh chocolate should check the product name and packaging against the latest official recall notice.


Affected products should not be eaten. They should instead be handled according to the recall instructions and returned to the appropriate retailer where applicable.


### Disclaimer


This article is provided for general informational purposes only and is not medical advice. Product recall information, affected batches and official guidance can change or be updated. Consumers should check the latest information issued by the manufacturer, retailer, Food Standards Agency and NHS. If you are unwell or concerned about your health after consuming a recalled product, contact an appropriate healthcare professional or medical service.
